info.title: PersonalFi API
info.description: Self-hosted personal finance and advisory. Single user, zero public ingress. Errors are RFC 9457 problem details; clients switch on `code`, never on `detail`.

type.description: Stable URI identifying the problem kind.

title.description: Short, human-readable summary. Does not change per occurrence.

code.description: Stable machine code the client switches on.

correlationId.description: Quote this when reporting the failure.

minor.description: Minor units as a decimal string. Never a JSON number.

MoneyInput.description: An amount of money. Negative is an outflow.

current.description: Contribution to net worth. A card you owe on is negative.

limit.description: A magnitude, not a contribution: always positive.

mask.description: Last 2-4 digits. Never the full number.

balance.description: null until a balance has been observed.

asOf.description: The oldest balance the totals rest on.

NetWorthInput.description: Net worth from the latest balance of every included account, per currency. `inputs` is the audit trail: every account, whether it counted, and why not.

bootstrapped.description: Whether a user account exists yet.

fresh.description: Whether a step-up assertion is still within its window.

name.description: For error messages and provenance. Never parsed.

format.description: Sniffed from the content if absent.

presetId.description: One of the built-in column mappings. Mutually exclusive with `profile`.

profile.description: A hand-built CSV mapping profile, when no preset fits.

account.description: Required for CSV and QIF, which carry no account identity of their own.

relinked.description: True when this replaced the credential on an existing row.

syncJobId.description: The queued backfill, when one was queued.

syncRunId.description: The completed backfill, when it ran inline.

mode.description: `inline` means the adapter stages in this process and could not be queued.

deduped.description: A sync of this connection was already queued or running.

maxSeq.description: Highest event sequence, as a string: it is a bigint.

maxLagEvents.description: Events the furthest-behind consumer has not read.

failedConsumers.description: Consumers stopped at an event they cannot handle.

stalled.description: Running jobs whose worker stopped heartbeating.

factId.description: The provider fact the current numbers were resolved from.

name.description: The resolved payee: the user’s name, else the provider’s.

excluded.description: The user took this out of budgets and totals.

supersededById.description: Set when another row supersedes this one. Marked, never hidden.

TransactionInput.description: A transaction as the reader resolves it: provider fact plus user overlay. The provider’s own numbers are under `provenance` in the detail endpoint.

revision.description: How many times the provider has restated this row.

factId.description: The provider fact the current numbers were resolved from.

name.description: The resolved payee: the user’s name, else the provider’s.

excluded.description: The user took this out of budgets and totals.

supersededById.description: Set when another row supersedes this one. Marked, never hidden.

totals.description: Summed per currency, transfers excluded. Never summed across currencies.

payeeName.description: The user’s name for the payee. `null` restores the provider’s.

get.description: Always answers if the process is running. Does not touch the database.

Reports 503 until the database is reachable and every migration is applied. Outbox lag and queue health are reported in the body and mark the service `degraded` without, by default, failing the probe.
Reports whether the encryption key is available and whether a user exists. Answers while the application is locked, which is what makes a future unlock page possible.

post.description: Supply the one-time enrolment token from `just bootstrap-user`, or call with a session that has stepped up in the last five minutes to add a second authenticator.

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

response.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Returns a challenge with an empty `allowCredentials`: discoverable credentials give usernameless login, and an empty list tells an unauthenticated caller nothing about which authenticators exist.

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

response.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.summary: Log in with the TOTP fallback
post.description: Secondary factor. The resulting session is deliberately not step-up fresh, so it cannot read a provider credential without a passkey assertion first.

post.summary: Log in with a single-use recovery code

options.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Marks the session fresh for five minutes.

response.description: A WebAuthn response as produced by @simplewebauthn/browser.

post.description: Single-use. Presenting a refresh token that has already been rotated revokes the entire session family: that is the cookie-theft signal.

delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion. The last remaining passkey cannot be removed.

post.description: Returns the seed once. It is sealed with SecretBox before it reaches the database, so this response is the only place it is ever readable.

post.summary: Confirm TOTP enrolment with a generated code

post.description: Replaces any existing set. The codes are returned once and are Argon2id-hashed at rest; there is no way to see them again.

get.summary: Every account, with its latest balance
get.description: Closed accounts are hidden by default. They keep every transaction they ever had — "delete the account" and "stop showing me this account" are different requests.

patch.summary: Include an account in net worth, or close it
patch.description: The two fields a user owns. An account name comes from the provider and is not editable in Phase 1 — there is no nickname column yet (see the WP 1.5 evidence note).

get.description: Totals are reported per currency and never summed across them: there is no FX table in Phase 1, and adding dollars to euros would be a wrong number rendered confidently.

Keyset pagination over `(date DESC, id DESC)`. Pass `nextCursor` back verbatim; it is opaque and a client that parses it will break. `summary` is returned on the first page of a filter (no `cursor`) and is `null` on subsequent pages.
Needs a step-up assertion (decision D21). A stolen session cookie must not be enough to walk out with the complete history. Accepts the same filters as the list.

get.summary: One transaction, with provenance, splits and its transfer link

patch.description: Provider facts are immutable. This writes intent — note, category, exclusion, payee name — which the resolver layers over the fact and which survives every re-sync.

post.summary: Apply one overlay patch to many transactions
post.description: One transaction, so a bulk categorise is one undo entry and one toast (05 §5.3). An id that does not exist fails the whole batch rather than being skipped silently.
Replaces the existing splits wholesale. The lines must sum to the transaction, to the cent, in its currency: a set that does not is `ledger.splits_do_not_sum` (422).

post.summary: Confirm that two rows are one movement of money
post.description: Confidence 1.0 and `user_confirmed`: this is not a heuristic. Any standing rejection of the same pair is withdrawn, so the next pairing run does not silently refuse to re-propose what the user just confirmed.

post.summary: Say no to a transfer pairing, permanently
post.description: `transactionId` is **either leg** of the pair; the other is read from the link. The rejection is recorded as well as undone, so the heuristic does not re-propose it.

otherTransactionId.description: Required only when the two rows are not currently linked.

get.summary: Every provider this deployment can link
get.description: The "Add a connection" screen, as data. A new adapter appears here by being registered at the composition root; no UI change is required (08 §2.7).

get.summary: Every connection, with status and freshness
get.description: No credential appears in this payload — not as a field, not as a redacted placeholder, not as a boolean called `hasToken`. `status` plus `errorSince` is what the UI actually needs to say "stale for 26 hours".

post.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). `input` is opaque and validated by the adapter — a Plaid public token, a set of manual accounts, a file upload descriptor. A union here would have to grow with every provider and would be wrong the first time one changed its link flow. Re-linking an institution already connected updates that row and preserves its cursor and accounts; it never creates a second one.

get.summary: One connection, its accounts and its recent runs

delete.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21). Revokes at the provider best-effort, then destroys the local credential — the local half always happens, because a provider that is down must not be able to stop a user from disconnecting. **Accounts, transactions and the sync history are kept**: "disconnect" and "delete my data" are different requests and only one of them is reversible. `revokedAtProvider: false` means we could not tell the provider; with Plaid the Item still occupies a billing slot until it is removed there, so the UI should say so.

providerSlotMayRemain.description: True when revocation failed: the provider may still hold the item.

post.summary: Finish a link whose flow ran in the browser
post.description: The second half of a provider-hosted flow (08 §3.6): the user came back from Plaid Link with a public token and this exchanges it. Needs a step-up assertion. The resulting connection must be the one named in the path, or this is a 409 — silently creating a second connection under the first one’s URL is how a net worth doubles.

post.summary: Replace the credential on an existing connection
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion: a new credential is an addition, not a read. The cursor and every mapped account survive, which is the whole point — 08 §3.9, "losing account identity on reconnect is the classic way a personal finance app silently doubles a user’s net worth". `reconnectFlow` on the connector says what the UI should have collected: `provider_hosted`, `credential_form`, `reupload` or `none`.

relinked.description: True when this replaced the credential on an existing row.

syncJobId.description: The queued backfill, when one was queued.

syncRunId.description: The completed backfill, when it ran inline.

post.description: Returns the queued work, never the result: the result is in `sync_runs` and on the event stream. Deduped and singleton on the connection — a webhook, the nightly schedule and an impatient user cannot start three cursor loops on one connection, which 04 §4.4 calls "the fastest way to corrupt cursor state".

get.description: 08 §6.3: "`sync_runs` is the observability surface that matters… this single feature eliminates most 'why is my balance wrong' debugging". Every attempt leaves a row, including the ones that failed before the first page.

post.summary: Import a CSV, OFX/QFX or QIF file
post.description: Creates a file-import connection on the first upload and stages onto it thereafter, then runs the import **synchronously** — a file upload has no meaningful "come back later", and the adapter stages in this process (see the module comment). Re-importing the same file changes nothing: every row is identified by a hash of its own content, and the ledger’s natural key catches whatever the staging layer misses.

connectionId.description: Omit to create a new file-import connection.

skipped.description: Rows already staged by an earlier upload.

post.summary: A Plaid Link token for a new connection
post.description: Step one of a provider-hosted link (08 §3.6): the pins are `PlaidConnector`'s own (products transactions+investments+liabilities, 730 days, PFC v2, the configured redirect_uri) — see wp1.3-plaid.md §1. Read-only: nothing in this application changes as a result of calling it.

post.summary: Finish a Plaid Link flow and create the connection
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion (D21) — this is the moment a real credential is stored, exactly like `POST /connections`. Exchanges the public token, creates (or re-links) the connection, and schedules the first sync through the orchestrator. Refuses an eleventh Plaid connection (D16: Trial's 10-Item cap; `/item/remove` does not free a slot, so this counts every Plaid row ever created, including a disconnected one).

institutionName.description: From Link's own metadata; falls back to /item/get when omitted.

post.summary: A Plaid Link token in update mode, for reconnect
post.description: Needs a step-up assertion: it opens the connection's sealed credential to build the request. 01 §1.7: "the access_token does not change when using Link in update mode" — no `products` on the wire (a `products` array in update mode re-initialises the Item's product set and can re-bill it — wp1.3-plaid.md §1), and nothing here needs re-sealing. Completing the reauth still goes through the existing `POST /connections/{id}/reconnect`.

accountSelectionEnabled.description: 01 §1.7: any de-selected account stops being shared. Off by default so a routine reauth cannot silently drop an account.

get.description: `text/event-stream`. Events: `connection.created`, `connection.status`, `sync.progress`, `sync.completed`, `account.upserted`, `balance.recorded`. A `:` comment every 15 seconds keeps a proxy from reaping an idle stream. `id:` is the outbox sequence; send it back as `Last-Event-ID` (or `?from=`) to resume.

The link-flow stream: opened after `POST /connections` so the UI can follow the backfill. Carries the three events whose aggregate is a connection — `connection.created`, `connection.status`, `sync.completed`. Per-row progress is aggregated on an account and is on `/sync/stream`.

tags.description: Passkeys, TOTP fallback, recovery codes, sessions and step-up. Tokens travel in `__Host-` cookies and never in a response body.

tags.name: accounts
tags.description: Accounts, their latest balances, and net worth. Every balance says when.

tags.name: transactions
tags.description: The feed, the overlay, splits, transfers and the CSV export. Pagination is keyset: pass `nextCursor` back verbatim.

tags.name: connections
tags.description: Providers, the link and reconnect flows, sync history, and the server-sent event streams that carry sync progress.
